Let the tangent line to the unit circle be written in normal form
$$l:\ x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta=1,$$
where $(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)$ is the point of tangency.  
Since $l$ meets both coordinate axes, $\sin\theta\neq 0$ and $\cos\theta\neq 0$, and the intercepts are
$$N=(\sec\theta,0),\qquad M=(0,\csc\theta).$$

With $A(3,4)$ and $C(0,0)$ we have
$$\overrightarrow{AC}=(-3,-4),\quad \overrightarrow{AM}=(-3,\csc\theta-4),\quad \overrightarrow{AN}=(\sec\theta,-4).$$

Writing $\overrightarrow{AC}=x\overrightarrow{AM}+y\overrightarrow{AN}$ and solving the resulting linear system yields
$$x=\frac{4\sin\theta}{\,4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta-1\,},\qquad 
y=\frac{3\cos\theta}{\,4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta-1\,}.$$

Therefore, for $P(x,y)$,
$$9x^{2}+16y^{2}
=\frac{144\sin^{2}\theta+144\cos^{2}\theta}{(4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta-1)^{2}}
=\frac{144}{(4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta-1)^{2}}.$$

Now $4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta=5\sin(\theta+\varphi)$ (with $\cos\varphi=\tfrac45$, $\sin\varphi=\tfrac35$), so
$$4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta\in[-5,5].$$
Hence $4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta-1\in[-6,4]$, and the denominator satisfies
$$(4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta-1)^{2}\le 6^{2}=36,$$
with equality when $4\sin\theta+3\cos\theta=-5$ (e.g. $\sin\theta=-\tfrac45$, $\cos\theta=-\tfrac35$, which gives a valid tangent intersecting both axes).

Thus the minimum value is
$$\min(9x^{2}+16y^{2})=\frac{144}{36}=4.$$

\boxed{4}
